title: Establish per-GPU cold/warm-start profile artifacts and pin heuristics for model onboarding
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Produce a standardized artifact set and decision rules that capture both cold-start and warm-start latency/throughput behavior for each target GPU SKU (A100, H100, L40S, MI300) during model onboarding. These artifacts will drive: model version pin recommendations, warmup batch sizing, KV-cache warmup guidance, and an automated annotation that gets published to the model's performance profile registry.

Why: Current model onboarding publishes single steady-state numbers that hide transient behavior. Customers building interactive products (chat, assistants) see variable latency during ramp-up windows or under KV cache churn. We need reproducible cold/warm signatures to: (1) make pin decisions safer, (2) suggest warmup strategies to customers/Dedicated, and (3) enable routing policies that consider transient tail latency.

Scope:
- Define standardized benchmark run (inputs, sequence lengths, context prefixes) to capture cold vs warm metrics.
- Collect artifacts for A100/H100/L40S/MI300 for a target model family (eg. llama-3-70b and a smaller 7B baseline) across quantization variants.
- Produce per-device CSV/JSON summary with: cold_p50/p95/p99, warm_p50/p95/p99 after N warm tokens, sustained throughput (tokens/s), recommended pin_label and pin_ttl heuristic.
- Define automated rule-set that maps artifact signatures to pin recommendation: pin to variant X when p99_warm < threshold AND variance < X, else suggest fallback policy.
- Add KV-cache warmup guide: number of tokens to reach 90% steady-state cache hit and recommended proactive warmup API calls.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Reproducible benchmark script checked into infra repo with a README and exact seed/config.
2) Artifacts for at least two models (1 large, 1 small) produced for each GPU SKU and uploaded to the performance profile registry.
3) Clear pin heuristic documentation that Product and Console teams can consume (doc + example mapping table).
4) One automated test that validates the artifact schema and the pin-rule outputs in CI.
5) Short rollout plan to annotate 5 newly onboarded models with the new artifacts in runtime-1.22 canary.

Non-goals: automated re-pinning in production (we will only surface recommendations), per-instance dynamic pinning logic.

Technical approach (high level):
- Benchmark harness: extend existing per-gpu-bench runner to add a warmup phase with controlled token streams and KV cache flush intervals.
- Samples: sample input prompts across 3 sequence-length buckets (64, 512, 2048) and repeat each 10x to measure warmup curve.
- Metrics: collect latency histograms, throughput, mem usage, and KV cache hit-rate over time. Postprocess to derive cold vs warm percentiles and a delta curve.
- Pin heuristics: implement a lightweight rule engine (YAML) that maps observed metrics to suggestions: {pin_variant, reason, expected_improvement_pct, suggested_warm_tokens}.

Tradeoffs and open questions:
- Cost vs coverage: full sweep across quantization and batch-size matrix is expensive. We'll prioritize the common customer variants (fp16, q4f16, q8) and reasonable batch sizes (1,4,8).
- TTL semantics: how long should a pin recommendation remain valid? Start conservative (30d) but include stability metadata to trigger re-evals.
- Interaction with routing: recommendations should be advisory for Console to consume; runtime routing policies may override.

Rollout plan:
- Week 1: finalize harness changes and schema, land infra PR.
- Week 2: run A100 and H100 sweeps for two models, produce artifacts.
- Week 3: L40S and MI300 runs, publish registry entries, create pin-rule YAMLs.
- Week 4: integrate docs, add CI validation, and annotate 5 canary models.

Links to artifacts and specs: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Per-GPU+Cold-Warm+Profile+Spec, https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1128, https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/bench/per-gpu-warmup?orgId=1
